title: prunus avium f. silvestris
intro: Prunus avium f. silvestris, commonly known as wild cherry, is a deciduous shrub or small tree belonging to the Rosaceae family. It is a wild variant of the cherry tree, characterized by its dark green leaves and fragrant flowers. The bark and leaves of Prunus avium f. silvestris have been traditionally used in herbal medicine for their health benefits, which include lowering fever, relieving coughs, and treating respiratory issues due to its expectorant properties. The bioactive constituents of this plant include salicin, a glycoside similar to aspirin, which contributes to its anti-inflammatory and analgesic actions, and flavonoids, such as kaempferol and quercetin, which have antioxidant properties.
